message.content:
**C♯ Major Scale**

The C♯ major scale follows the standard major‑scale pattern of whole–whole–half–whole–whole–whole–half steps.  
The notes are:

| Step | Note | (Enharmonic equivalent) |
|------|------|--------------------------|
| 1    | C♯   | –                        |
| 2    | D♯   | –                        |
| 3    | E♯   | F                        |
| 4    | F♯   | –                        |
| 5    | G♯   | –                        |
| 6    | A♯   | –                        |
| 7    | B♯   | C                        |
| 8    | C♯   | –                        |

So the full scale is:

**C♯ – D♯ – E♯ – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – B♯ – C♯**

(With the enharmonic equivalents E♯ ≈ F and B♯ ≈ C, you can also think of it as C♯ – D♯ – F – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – C – C♯.)

**Key signature:** 7 sharps (C♯, D♯, E♯, F♯, G♯, A♯, B♯).
